findings.issue: Global pairing tracks only button codes, so it can consume another pointer's release and lose the release it actually owns.
findings.evidence: Pointer A presses left on a bar: held[0] becomes true. Pointer B presses left outside the bar: that press passes. B releases first: PG calls onRelease(BTN_LEFT), cancels B's release and clears A's ownership. A's eventual release passes. Two consumed left presses likewise collapse into one boolean. The local Hyprland 0.57 InputManager.cpp:720 emits the plugin event before processing buttons and tracks subsequent held buttons by both button and pointer; it does not merge these events first. SButtonEvent omits pointer identity, and the new tests cover different buttons rather than this same-button/two-pointer case. This violates design.md's explicit origin/button pairing requirement.
findings.fix: Carry reliable pointer identity into the surviving pairing coordinator and track ownership by pointer and button. If the current event interface cannot provide identity, resolve that interface limitation explicitly before claiming this requirement complete. Add regressions for two pointers using the same button, including one passed press, both consumed presses, both release orders and originating-bar destruction.
